issues.legal_issue: A public purpose stated as execution of an interim development plan is sufficiently specific for acquisition of a large area when the plan may require different plots for different uses.
material_facts: The acquisition notification identified the purpose as execution of the Interim General Plan for the Greater Delhi.
The notification covered a large area of about 3,000 acres, potentially requiring different plots for different purposes under the plan.
The landowner had not objected before the authorities that the stated purpose was too vague to permit effective objections.
issues.conclusion: The stated purpose was specific in the circumstances and was not vague; the challenge on that ground also had not been raised before the High Court.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, the stated public purpose must be sufficiently specific in context. For a large area comprising many plots, the purpose may be stated by reference to a plan without identifying the particular use of every plot. The Court distinguished Munshi Singh v. Union of India and relied on Aflatoon v. Lt. Governor of Delhi and Ratni Devi v. Chief Commissioner.

rule.if: land_acquisition_challenge and purpose_identifies_development_plan and large_area_may_have_varied_uses and no_effective_objection_claim

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity of an acquisition of land.
predicates.purpose_identifies_development_plan: The notification identifies execution of a development plan as the purpose of the proposed acquisition.
predicates.large_area_may_have_varied_uses: The acquisition covers a large area whose different plots may be used for different purposes under the plan.
predicates.no_effective_objection_claim: The landowner did not claim that the stated purpose prevented the filing of effective objections.

issues.definition: When an acquisition challenge concerns a large area that may be used for varied purposes under an identified development plan, and no inability to object effectively is claimed, the stated purpose is sufficiently specific.

issues.legal_issue: Execution of an interim plan intended to prevent unplanned development and secure planned development serves a public purpose for land acquisition.
material_facts: The Interim General Plan was prepared and published by the Government after Cabinet approval as an interim development policy until a Master Plan could be completed.
The plan aimed to prevent haphazard and unplanned development and thereby ensure planned development.
The acquisition notification stated that the land was likely to be required for execution of that plan.
issues.conclusion: Execution of the Interim General Plan was a public purpose for the purposes of section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act permits notification of land likely to be required for a public purpose. Aflatoon v. Lt. Governor of Delhi held that planned development of Delhi is a public purpose; the Court applied that principle to an interim plan serving the same objective.

rule.if: land_acquisition_challenge and government_approved_interim_plan and plan_prevents_unplanned_development and acquisition_is_for_plan_execution

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity of an acquisition of land.
predicates.government_approved_interim_plan: The Government approved an interim development plan as a policy measure pending a more complete plan.
predicates.plan_prevents_unplanned_development: The plan is intended to prevent haphazard development and secure planned development.
predicates.acquisition_is_for_plan_execution: The proposed acquisition is for carrying out the plan.

issues.definition: When a land-acquisition challenge concerns an acquisition to execute a government-approved interim plan intended to prevent unplanned development, the acquisition purpose is public.

issues.legal_issue: The freezing effect that follows publication of an acquisition notification does not invalidate the acquisition when it is an inherent consequence of the notification.
material_facts: The landowner argued that the acquisition notification was issued for the collateral purpose of freezing the land.
Publication of the notification affected dealings with the land and the treatment of its value and improvements.
The notification stated that the acquisition was for execution of the Interim General Plan.
issues.conclusion: The freezing effect did not affect the validity of the notification or acquisition proceedings because that effect was inherent in publication of an acquisition notification.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, notification gives public notice of proposed acquisition and warns that later dealings are at the dealer’s risk. Sections 23 and 24 provide, respectively, for valuation by reference to the publication date and for disregarding certain post-notification outlays, improvements, or disposals. Those consequences make the freezing effect inherent in the statutory process.

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity of an acquisition of land.
predicates.notification_announces_proposed_acquisit: The notification publicly states that the land is proposed to be acquired.
predicates.land_freezing_follows_from_notification: The restriction or risk affecting dealings with the land follows from publication of the acquisition notification.

issues.definition: When a notification announces a proposed acquisition and the land-freezing effect follows from that notification, the effect does not invalidate the acquisition.

issues.legal_issue: The decision not to acquire some land covered by a notification does not by itself invalidate the acquisition of other land covered by the same notification.
material_facts: Some land that had also been proposed for acquisition under the notification was later excluded from acquisition.
The landowner argued that this exclusion undermined the validity of the acquisition of the land at issue.
The statutory objection process allowed interested persons to object, after which the Collector made recommendations and the Government decided whether to proceed.
issues.conclusion: The exclusion of other land did not militate against the validity of the acquisition of the land at issue.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5A of the Land Acquisition Act provides for objections by interested persons, a hearing and recommendations by the Collector, and a decision by the appropriate Government. The Government may accept some objections and reject others; the differing outcomes alone do not establish an inherent defect in the acquisition of other land.

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity of an acquisition of land.
predicates.other_notified_land_is_excluded: Some other land covered by the same acquisition notification is later not acquired.
predicates.objections_are_decided_for_individual_la: Objections to acquisition are considered and decided in relation to the land concerned.

issues.definition: When some other notified land is excluded after objections are considered for the land concerned, that exclusion does not invalidate the acquisition being challenged.

issues.legal_issue: An opportunity to be heard on acquisition objections is afforded when the objector is notified of a hearing, even if the objector does not establish that a representative attended.
material_facts: The company filed written objections to the proposed acquisition.
It was informed that the objections would be heard on a specified date at the Collector’s office.
The company did not establish through an affidavit or the relevant record that a representative attended the hearing.
The Collector’s report showed that objections were considered and recommendations were made, and the company’s written representation was in the file.
issues.conclusion: There was no force in the contention that the company had not been afforded an opportunity to be heard before the Collector made the report.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5A(2) of the Land Acquisition Act requires the Collector to give an objector an opportunity of being heard, to consider objections, and to report recommendations to the appropriate Government. The Court assessed whether that opportunity was afforded on the evidence in the case and did not treat an unproved claim of attendance as establishing that it was denied.

rule.if: land_acquisition_challenge and written_objections_filed and hearing_opportunity_notified and no_reliable_proof_of_attendance

predicates.land_acquisition_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity of an acquisition of land.
predicates.written_objections_filed: The landowner submits written objections to the proposed acquisition.
predicates.hearing_opportunity_notified: The objector is informed of a hearing at which the objections may be presented.
predicates.no_reliable_proof_of_attendance: The objector does not provide reliable evidence that a representative attended the hearing.

issues.definition: When written objections are filed and a hearing opportunity is notified, the opportunity is afforded even if the objector does not reliably establish attendance.
